Removal test (Law 8): remove symbols and the amulet ceases to operate — an amulet's power is entirely symbolic, deriving its function from the symbolic meanings assigned to it. Without symbolic interpretation, an amulet is just an object with no function.

Liturgy is a formal, structured form of ritual — the word itself derives from Greek leitourgia (public work). Ritual is the broader practice; liturgy is the codified, scripted version. Epochs confirm ritual (0.81) predates liturgy (0.88).

colophon is a specific kind of paratext — a brief inscription at the end of a book or manuscript providing production details. A competent speaker calls a colophon 'a type of paratext'. Epochs: paratext (0.15) predates colophon (0.69).

palimpsest is a specific kind of manuscript — a page or scroll scraped clean and reused for writing. A competent speaker calls it 'a type of manuscript'. Epochs: manuscript (0) predates palimpsest (0.69).

For-whose-sake test (Law 8d): knowledge-management is designed and maintained for the sake of decision-making. Organizations invest in KM systems, processes, and practices specifically so that decision-makers have access to the right knowledge at the right time. The servant (KM) points at the master (decision-making).
Liturgy is designed and maintained for the sake of religion (Law 8d): it is the codified, scripted form of religious practice, structured for the performance and perpetuation of religious ritual.
Removal test (Law 8): remove symbols and notation ceases to operate — notation IS a system of symbols. Symbols are constitutive to notation's function (Law 8b: this is operating, not merely sayable).

A numerical method is a specific kind of algorithm — a step-by-step procedure for numerical computation. A competent speaker would call a numerical method 'a kind of algorithm.' Law 9: specific→general. Algorithm is the nearest kind (more specific than 'procedure' or 'method').
refutation is a specific kind of argument — one aimed at disproof of a claim. Law 9: competent speaker calls refutation 'a type/kind of argument'. Direction: specific(refutation)→general(argument).

reductionism is a specific kind of methodology — approaching complex systems by breaking them into simpler parts. Law 9: competent speaker calls reductionism 'a methodology/methodological approach'. Direction: specific(reductionism)→general(methodology).

A caveat is a specific kind of caution — a formal warning, limitation, or stipulation attached to an agreement, statement, or action. Law 9: a competent speaker would call a caveat 'a type of caution.' Direction: specific(caveat)→general(caution).

footnote is a specific kind of annotation — one placed at the bottom of a page (as opposed to marginal or inline). Law 9: a competent speaker calls a footnote 'a kind of annotation.' Direction: specific→general. Pin sense: annotation = textual addition providing supplementary information.

incipit is the opening words of a literary work — traditionally a book. Law 8 removal test: remove books and the incipit (as a literary convention of opening text) ceases to operate; it becomes just random words. Direction: incipit needs book to function as its concept. Pin sense: incipit = opening words of a written work.

palimpsest is a manuscript that has been scraped clean and reused for writing. Law 8 removal test: remove manuscripts and the palimpsest ceases to operate — it is literally a condition OF a manuscript. Direction: palimpsest needs manuscript to function. Pin sense: palimpsest = a manuscript with overwritten text layers.

Apostrophe IS a specific kind of rhetorical device — it addresses an absent person, abstract concept, or inanimate object as though present. Law 9: specific→general; a competent speaker calls apostrophe 'a rhetorical device.' Pinned sense: the rhetorical figure, not the celestial bodies.

A micrometer needs measurement to operate — it is a tool FOR measurement. Removal test: remove measurement (the practice/concept) and the micrometer ceases to function as anything other than a metal object. The tool's operation depends on the practice. Direction: micrometer→measurement (newer→older).

A gloss IS a specific kind of annotation: a brief explanatory note on a word or term. Law 9: a competent speaker would call a gloss 'an annotation.' The note pins the sense of annotation as any explanatory marginal or inline comment.

A micrometer IS a specific kind of tool — a precision measuring tool. Law 9: a competent speaker would call a micrometer 'a tool.' No nearer kind (measuring-instrument) exists, so this is the nearest INSTANCE_OF per Law 11e.

exemplar INSTANCE_OF model: an exemplar is a specific kind of model used as a standard of excellence. A competent speaker would call an exemplar 'a model.' Direction: exemplar (specific) → model (general). Epochs confirm model (0.04) predates exemplar (0.38), consistent with this being INSTANCE_OF rather than DERIVED_FROM.

errata INSTANCE_OF record: errata is a specific kind of record — a published list of corrections to a work. A competent speaker would call errata 'a record of errors.' Direction: errata (specific) → record (general). Epochs confirm record (0) predates errata (0.69).

stakeholder INSTANCE_OF role: a stakeholder is a specific kind of role — a person holding a position of interest in a project or organization. A competent speaker calls a stakeholder 'a role' in the project. Direction: stakeholder (specific) → role (general).

nomogram DEPENDS_ON mathematics: remove mathematics from a nomogram and it stops operating as a calculation device — the aligned scales, logarithmic relationships, and functional mappings are pure mathematical constructs. The which-came-first test: the mathematical relationship must exist for the nomogram to function at all.

Numerical-method DEPENDS_ON mathematics: remove mathematics and numerical methods stop operating entirely. Numerical methods are computational techniques for solving mathematical problems (root-finding, integration, differential equations, linear systems). Their algorithms, convergence criteria, error bounds, and all their operations are defined in mathematical terms. Without mathematics, numerical methods are not merely unsayable — they cease to function as procedures for approximate mathematical computation. The removal test passes: X needs Y to operate now (Law 8, 8b).

Sense: gauge as measuring device (not as verification procedure). A vernier caliper is a specific type of precision measuring device that compares unknown dimensions against a known scale. Removal test (for DEPENDS_ON): remove the concept of 'gauge' and vernier-caliper loses its category — it is a kind of gauge. This is INSTANCE_OF: specific→nearest general kind.

gauge is a specific kind of tool — an artifact that extends human measurement capacity. INSTANCE_OF direction correct: specific to general. A competent speaker calls a gauge a tool. The removal test doesn't apply here — this is a kind relationship, not dependency.

gauge DEPENDS_ON measurement: apply the removal test — remove measurement (the practice and concept of assigning/comparing values) and a gauge stops operating entirely. A gauge's function IS to measure; without measurement, it is a meaningless object. This is a genuine present-tense operational dependency, not mere sayability.

Decision-cascade: remove evaluation (the practice of assessing against criteria) and a decision-cascade stops operating — each step in the cascade requires evaluation to decide whether to trigger the next. The removal test passes: without evaluation, the cascade has no mechanism to proceed.

Decision-tree: remove evaluation and a decision-tree stops operating — each node requires evaluating a condition to decide which branch to follow. Without evaluation, the tree is just structure with no function.

A nomogram is a graphical calculating device whose curves are constructed by interpolation between known reference values. Remove interpolation method — the curves cannot be constructed, and the nomogram stops operating. Removal test passes: X stops OPERATING without Y.

Interpolation is a mathematical procedure for estimating unknown values between known data points. Remove mathematics — the method has no theoretical basis, no algorithms, and stops operating. Removal test passes.

A cheat sheet is a condensed reference whose entire identity rests on information compression — maximal useful content in minimal space. Remove compression (the practice of reducing information density while preserving meaning) and a cheat sheet stops being distinguishable from any other document. Removal test passes: X stops OPERATING without Y.

Interpolation estimates values between known data points — those points come from measurement. Remove measurement and interpolation has no empirical data to operate on. This is a present-tense operational dependency, not a historical one.

A nomogram is a specific type of diagram: a graphical calculating device. A competent speaker would call a nomogram 'a diagram' — it uses visual marks to depict mathematical relationships. Specific→general INSTANCE_OF direction.

A cheat-sheet is a specific type of reference document designed for quick consultation. A competent speaker would call a cheat sheet 'a reference' — it provides condensed information for quick lookup. Specific→general INSTANCE_OF direction.
A flowchart is a specific type of diagram — it represents processes using visual symbols and arrows. A competent speaker would call a flowchart 'a diagram.' Specific→general INSTANCE_OF.
A histogram is a specific type of diagram — it visually encodes data distributions using bars. A competent speaker would call a histogram 'a diagram.' Specific→general INSTANCE_OF.

A protractor is a specific kind of measuring instrument — a competent speaker would call it 'a measuring instrument'. It measures angles, which is its function within the broader class of measuring tools.
angle IS a specific kind of measurement — specifically, measurement of rotation between two lines/planes. A competent speaker would call an angle a measurement. Nearest kind: measurement.

A protractor's function is to measure angles — its physical scales and arc are calibrated in degrees and radians. Remove the concept of angle and a protractor becomes an unmarked piece of plastic that cannot operate for its intended purpose. The removal test passes: the instrument stops operating without the quantity it measures.

Theodolite is a specific kind of surveying-instrument: a precision device for measuring horizontal and vertical angles in surveying work. Theodolite IS a surveying-instrument per the category definition — a device calibrated to acquire spatial measurements using sensing elements and reference systems. Removal of surveying-instruments as a class: theodolite would have no category, though it still operates. This is INSTANCE_OF (Law 9), not DEPENDS_ON.

Scorecard DEPENDS_ON measurement because: measurement (epoch 0.08) predates scorecard (0.20). A scorecard's function is to record measurement results; without the measurement concept, it is merely paper with markings and cannot operate as intended. The removal test passes: remove measurement and the scorecard ceases to function.
Nomography is a specific kind of method — a graphical technique for solving mathematical equations. A competent speaker would say 'nomography is a method.' Nearest kind: method.
A slide rule is a specific kind of tool — a mechanical computing device that extends human calculation capacity. A competent speaker would say 'a slide rule is a tool.' Nearest kind: tool.
Surveying is a specific kind of method — a systematic procedure for determining spatial relationships. A competent speaker would say 'surveying is a method.' Nearest kind: method.

Geodesy needs surveying methods to operate now — its observation methods include terrestrial surveying as a core component. Remove surveying and geodesy loses its primary observational methodology. The removal test passes per Law 8.

Nomography is a specific graphical technique for solving equations. Mathematics existed first (ancient) and fed into the development of nomography as a specialized mathematical practice. Which-came-first test: mathematics predates nomography by millennia.

Remove measurement right now — does surveying stop operating? Yes. Surveying's entire function is to make precise measurements of spatial relationships. Without measurement, surveying has no operation. The removal test passes cleanly.

Remove diagrams right now — does nomography stop operating? Yes. Nomography IS the practice of solving equations via calibrated graphical plots. Without diagrams, nomography ceases to function. The removal test passes.

Nomography solves equations through calibrated graphical plots. Remove mathematics and the equations it operates on cease to exist — nomography has no substance without the mathematical relationships it visualizes. The removal test: no mathematics = no equations = nomography stops operating entirely.

A theodolite is a precision instrument designed to measure horizontal and vertical angles. Remove the concept of angle and the theodolite's measurement function ceases to operate — it literally measures angles. The removal test passes: no angle concept = no function for a theodolite.

Surveying operates through geometric and trigonometric calculations — triangulation, coordinate computation, area/volume determination all require mathematics. Remove mathematics and surveying's calculation methodology ceases to operate. The removal test passes: no math = no surveying.

Angle is a geometric concept that quantifies rotation or inclination. Remove measurement right now and the angle concept ceases to operate — angle is fundamentally about measuring rotation. The removal test passes. Direction: angle depends on measurement as a concept.

A prologue is a preliminary section of a literary or dramatic work. Remove narrative right now and the prologue concept ceases to operate — a prologue only exists to set up or frame a narrative. The removal test passes. Direction: prologue depends on narrative.

Geodesy is a specific kind of science — a scientific discipline that measures and models the Earth. Per Law 9, specific→general: a competent speaker would say 'geodesy is a science.' Nearest kind: science.

Remove mathematics right now and logarithm ceases to operate — logarithms are mathematical concepts (exponents, bases, functions). Mathematics is constitutive of logarithm's operation, not merely historical association. Removal test passes.
Angle is a specific kind of concept — a geometric concept that quantifies rotation or inclination. A competent speaker would call angle 'a concept.' Direction specific→general per Law 9.
Prologue is a specific kind of concept — a literary concept representing a preliminary section. A competent speaker would call a prologue 'a concept.' Direction specific→general per Law 9.

A scorecard is a specific kind of tool — an artifact extending human capacity for recording and evaluating scores. Per Law 11c, passive artifacts qualify as tools: 'a shelf IS a tool.' A competent speaker would call a scorecard 'a tool for recording/evaluating.' The nearest kind available.

Logarithm needs number to operate now: a logarithm is the exponent for a base and argument within the number system. Remove number right now and the logarithm concept ceases to function — it has no operands, no base, no value. The removal test passes at object level (Law 8): this is not the meta-level 'all concepts need number' shadow (Law 2b) but a genuine operational dependency of logarithm on the number system.

Removal test (Law 8): a flowchart is a visual diagram showing steps and decisions. Remove diagram (the visual representation convention) and a flowchart ceases to operate — it is fundamentally a diagrammatic form. This is about operating, not sayability (Law 8b). Direction: diagram is older than flowchart (chronologically).
A scorecard is a specific kind of record — one that tracks scores and points over time. A competent speaker would call a scorecard 'a record' of game/play. Specific→general per Law 9.

A scorecard needs notation to operate now — it records scores via symbolic representation. Remove notation and a scorecard has no way to represent information. Per Law 8's removal test, this is a genuine dependency, not mere historical association.

Removal test (Law 8): a nomogram maps numerical quantities to scale positions to reveal mathematical relationships. Remove measurement and there are no quantities to map — nomography stops operating. This is not meta-level sayability but object-level function: nomography needs measurement to function. The note tests removal of the target and shows collapse of the source.

Removal test (Law 8): liminal-space is the concept of being at a transitional boundary. Remove threshold and the notion of liminality vanishes — there is no boundary to be between. Liminal space operates only through the concept of threshold as its structural reference point.

Removal test (Law 8): angle IS the concept of measured rotation. Remove measurement — the quantification of magnitude — and angle ceases to operate as a concept: there is nothing to measure, no scale to apply the angle to. The geometric figure of two rays exists naturally, but the MAP of angle (the entry per Law 2a) is constituted by the practice of measuring angular extent. Without measurement, angle is just lines on a page — the concept stops operating.

Removal test (Law 8): the theodolite operates as a device for measuring angles. Remove measurement and the theodolite has no function — it cannot operate without the concept of measurement. This is not meta-level (Law 2b): the theodolite's actual working, not just its sayability, requires measurement. Remove measurement and the theodolite is an inert tripod with lenses.

Triangulation IS a specific kind of method — a competent speaker calls it 'a method' for determining position or verifying information through multiple independent reference points. Specific→general per Law 9. Used in surveying, navigation, research.

Comparison IS a specific kind of method — a competent speaker calls it 'a method' of analysis. It is a structured technique for examining similarities and differences between entities. Specific→general per Law 9.

A siglum IS a symbol — specifically, a letter or abbreviation used as a shorthand reference to identify manuscripts in scholarly citation. Specific→general per Law 9. A competent speaker would say 'a siglum is a symbol used in citations.'
A cartogram IS a specific kind of map — a map where geographic area is distorted to represent a variable (population, GDP, etc.). Specific→general per Law 9.
A siglum IS a specific kind of abbreviation — a letter or short form used as shorthand to identify manuscripts in scholarly citation. Specific→general per Law 9.

A box plot IS a specific kind of diagram — specifically, a statistical diagram. A competent speaker would call a box plot 'a diagram' (specifically, a statistical diagram). Specific→general per Law 9. The accepted definition of 'diagram' (structural/relational/procedural visual representation) covers what a box plot does: it visually represents the distribution structure of data.

An isarithm IS a specific kind of map feature — a line-based map construct. A competent speaker in cartography would classify an isarithm as a type of map element/map. Specific→general per Law 9. Isarithms exist only within maps, making them map instances.

isarithm is a contour line connecting equal values on a map. Remove maps — the constructed spatial representation — and isarithm as a concept stops operating entirely. The removal test passes: isarithm needs map as its medium of existence.
An isarithm is a specific type of graph — a contour line used to graphically represent equal values on a map. Specific → general per Law 9.

An incipit (the opening words/letters of a text) derived from the practice of manuscript writing (manuscript epoch 0, incipit epoch 0.69). Which-came-first test passes: manuscripts predate incipits by millennia. The concept of incipit is a convention of manuscript/paginated text.

Remove books from the world right now and catchwords — words placed at the bottom of pages for pagination verification — lose all function. The removal test passes: catchwords operate only within the practice of book production. Catchword (epoch 0.15) predates book (0.73), but present-day dependency doesn't require which-came-first.
scatter plot is a specific type of graph: a plot using Cartesian coordinates to display values from two variables. Specific→general per Law 9.

A heatmap IS a specific kind of graph — it encodes data as a color-coded visual grid. Specific→general per Law 9. A competent speaker would call a heatmap 'a kind of graph' when viewing encoded data visually.
Contour lines (connecting equal-value points on a map) require a map to operate on — remove maps and contour lines cease to function as a cartographic convention. The removal test (Law 8) passes.
Data visualization encodes information into visual form — a specific kind of graph or graphical representation. Specific→general per Law 9.
Line chart displays data as connected points on axes — a specific kind of graph. Specific→general per Law 9.

Choropleth is a specific kind of thematic map — a competent cartographer calls it a map. The choropleth divides geographic regions and shades them by statistical value, which is precisely one mode of map-making. Per Law 9: 'is a specific kind of Y' → INSTANCE_OF. The direction is correct: choropleth (specific) → map (general).

A line chart IS a specific kind of data visualization. It plots data points connected by lines on a coordinate system — a specific mode of representing information visually. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.
A box plot IS a specific kind of data visualization. It displays statistical summaries through a visual box-and-whiskers representation on a coordinate system. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

Contour (lines) IS a specific kind of data visualization — it represents quantitative values (elevation) through visual marks (curved lines on a map). A competent cartographer would call contour a visualization method. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

A recension (critical comparison of textual variants) depends on the concept of a lemma — a key proposition or passage that serves as the reference point for the review. Remove lemma and recension has no anchor point to operate.

A box plot IS a specific kind of graph — it renders statistical data through geometric shapes (box, whiskers, outliers) on a coordinate system. A competent statistician calls it a graph. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

Data visualization is a specific kind of visualization — it applies the general practice of making information perceptible to the specific domain of data and information. Per Law 9: 'a competent speaker would call data visualization a visualization.' The direction is correct: data visualization (specific, domain-limited) → visualization (general, applies to all perceptible representations).

A heatmap IS a specific kind of data visualization — it encodes data values as colors in a grid to reveal patterns. A competent analyst calls it a visualization method. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

A lemma IS an argumentative proposition whose designed purpose is to serve argument — it exists to help establish an argument. Law 8d: 'for whose sake?' The servant (lemma) points at the master (argument). Remove argument and a lemma loses its purpose (it stops SERVEING argument), but lemma does not DEPEND_ON argument (a lemma can exist as a proposition without being deployed in argument). This is teleology, not dependency.

Parallel coordinates is a specific kind of graph used for multivariate data visualization. Tested: INSTANCE_OF — a competent speaker would call a parallel coordinates plot a type of graph. The graph is the nearest accepted kind (chart does not exist yet).
Remove ground-truth right now — measurement stops operating: without a known reference to compare against, measurement cannot validate or calibrate results. The removal test passes.

A lemma IS a specific kind of proposition — a proposition that is used as a stepping stone to prove a larger theorem. A competent speaker in logic/math classifies a lemma as a type of proposition. Nearest kind: proposition.

Ground-truth IS a specific kind of reference — namely, a reference point that serves as the ultimate validation standard against which measurements, claims, or models are checked. A competent speaker would call ground-truth a type of reference. Nearest kind: reference.

Pie chart IS a specific kind of data visualization — it displays data as proportions of a whole through circular slices. Per Law 9, a competent speaker calls a pie chart 'a data visualization.' Filing against the nearest kind.
Small multiples is a specific charting technique (Tufte) displaying multiple similar graphs side-by-side with a shared scale — it is a kind of data visualization, not the whole discipline.

Donut chart is a specific chart form (pie chart variant with a center hole) — a kind of data visualization. It encodes proportions as angular segments, making it a specific instance of the general category.
Lululemon is a specific athletic apparel company/brand. It is a kind of clothing brand — a competent speaker would call it 'a clothing brand.' INSTANCE_OF direction (specific→general) is correct.

Socks are a specific type of clothing brand product. A competent speaker calls socks 'a clothing item/brand product' — specific→general per Law 9. Direction: socks (specific) → clothing brand (general).

A bar chart is a specific type of data visualization. A competent speaker calls a bar chart 'a data visualization' — specific→general per Law 9. Direction: bar chart (specific) → data visualization (general).

A radial tree IS a specific kind of tree diagram — it represents the same hierarchical structure as a tree diagram but with a radial (circular) layout instead of linear. A competent speaker would classify a radial tree as a type of tree diagram. Law 9 specific→general.
An area chart IS a specific kind of data visualization — it represents quantitative data using areas on a coordinate system. A competent speaker would classify an area chart as a data visualization.
A stacked area chart is a specific kind of area chart that shows multiple data series stacked vertically — a competent speaker would classify it as a type of area chart per Law 9.

A flowchart is a specific kind of diagram that represents processes or workflows using nodes and arrows. When structured as a tree (decision trees, process trees), it is a specific kind of tree diagram per Law 9.

Refactoring IS a specific kind of process: a structured method of changing the internal organization of a system without altering its external behavior. A competent speaker classifies refactoring as 'a process.' Specific→general per Law 9. The removal test (Law 8) does not apply here — this is INSTANCE_OF, not DEPENDS_ON.

A dashboard IS a specific kind of diagram: a visual arrangement of information designed for quick comprehension. A competent speaker would call it 'a diagram' of performance or status. Specific→general per Law 9.

Dashboard IS a specific kind of data visualization: a composite display of multiple data points arranged for rapid comprehension. A competent speaker classifies a dashboard as 'a data visualization' or more precisely a dashboard IS a visual presentation of data — the specific kind of multi-metric display used in operational contexts. Law 9 INSTANCE_OF, specific→general.

A radar chart IS a specific kind of data visualization: it encodes multi-dimensional quantitative data into a two-dimensional graphic with multiple radial axes. Per Law 9, a competent speaker classifies a radar chart as 'a data visualization' — specifically, a chart type for comparing multiple variables across categories.

Sankey diagram IS a specific kind of data visualization that represents flows between entities with proportional-width arrows. Per Law 9, a competent speaker calls a sankey diagram a data visualization type. Direction: sankey diagram (epoch 1) is newer than data visualization (epoch 0.04), consistent with specific→general.

A recension (a critical edition comparing manuscript variants) DEPENDS_ON language because without language there is no text to compare, no critical apparatus to construct, and no scholarly communication about variants. The removal test: remove language, and recension cannot operate.

A venn diagram IS a specific kind of diagram. A competent speaker would call a venn diagram 'a diagram'. The specific (venn diagram) points to the general (diagram) per Law 9. Venn diagrams use overlapping shapes to visually represent logical relationships — this is a particular diagrammatic convention.
A treemap IS a specific kind of data visualization that represents hierarchical data using nested rectangles sized by values. Specific→general per Law 9.

A ladder IS a specific kind of classification structure — a hierarchical ordering of categories or types. In the context of the Constructum, ladders organize taxonomy levels from broad to specific. Specific→general per Law 9.
Bubble chart is a specific kind of data visualization. Sense: visual encoding using circles.
A violin plot is a specific kind of data visualization technique that visualizes distributions. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.
A waterfall chart is a specific kind of data visualization showing cumulative effects. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

Error bar is a specific kind of data visualization encoding that represents quantitative uncertainty. Direction specific→general per Law 9. A competent speaker classifies error bars as a data visualization technique.

Spider chart is a specific kind of data visualization technique for multivariate data. Direction specific→general per Law 9. A competent speaker would call a spider chart a form of data visualization.

Scatter plot matrix is a specific kind of data visualization — a grid of scatter plots showing pairwise relationships across multiple variables. Direction specific→general per Law 9: a competent speaker classifies a scatter plot matrix as a type of data visualization.

Stem plot is a specific kind of data visualization that displays individual data points as stems on a number line. Direction specific→general per Law 9: a competent speaker classifies a stem plot as a form of data visualization.

Contour plot is a specific kind of data visualization that uses contour lines to represent 3D surfaces on a 2D plane. Direction specific→general per Law 9: a competent speaker classifies a contour plot as a form of data visualization.

A dot plot is a specific kind of data visualization that uses dots on a number line to show frequency/distribution. Direction specific→general per Law 9: a competent speaker would call a dot plot 'a form of data visualization.'

A sunburst diagram is a specific kind of data visualization that represents hierarchical data as a group of nested rectangles. Law 9: specific→general — a competent speaker calls it a form of data visualization.
A gantt chart is a specific kind of diagram used for project scheduling. Tested Law 9: specific→general direction. A competent speaker calls a gantt chart a diagram — a bar chart arranged by time.

A recension is a specific kind of method for revising and standardizing texts in textual scholarship. Law 9: specific→general. A textual recension IS a method — a systematic approach to comparing and reconciling textual variants.
A chord diagram IS a specific kind of data visualization — a graphic showing interconnections between pairs of nodes using curved chords. Law 9 specific→general direction.

A word cloud IS a specific kind of data visualization — it encodes text frequency as visual prominence (font size, color) across a coordinate space. Law 9: specific→general. A competent speaker calls a word cloud 'a kind of data visualization.'

Streamgraph is a specific kind of data visualization — a stacked area chart variant with central baseline displacement. A competent speaker would call it a data visualization. Specific→general per Law 9.
Mosaic plot is a specific kind of data visualization: a graphical representation of multivariate categorical data using rectangles whose area is proportional to frequency. Specific→general per Law 9.

Trellis plot is a specific kind of data visualization: a grid of small multiple charts sharing the same variable encoding. A competent speaker would call it 'a data visualization'. Specific→general per Law 9.

Alluvial diagram is a specific kind of data visualization: a flow-based chart showing changes in categories over time using flowing bands. A competent speaker would call it 'a data visualization'. Specific→general per Law 9.

A streamgraph is a specific kind of data visualization: a flow-based chart showing changes in categories over time using stacked area graphs. A competent speaker would call it a data visualization. Specific→general per Law 9.

A lollipop chart IS a specific kind of data visualization: it encodes quantitative data using lines and circles to show values across categories. A competent speaker would call it a chart, which is a data visualization. Specific→general per Law 9.

A bump chart IS a specific kind of data visualization: it shows rank changes of items over time using horizontal bars positioned by rank. A competent speaker would classify it as a type of chart, which is a data visualization. Specific→general per Law 9.

A facet grid IS a specific kind of data visualization: it arranges multiple views of data into a grid where each cell is filtered by categorical variables. A competent speaker would call this a visualization technique. This is the nearest kind — facet grids are a method of data visualization.

A small multiple IS a specific kind of data visualization technique: it displays multiple subsets of the same data in a series of similar charts for comparison. A competent speaker would classify this as a type of data visualization layout.

A faceted visualization IS a specific kind of data visualization: it creates multiple coordinated views (facets) of the same or related data, each filtered by categorical variable values. A competent speaker calls it a visualization technique. Direction: specific→general. The facets grid and small multiple are specific instances of this general approach.

A forest plot IS a specific kind of data visualization: it arranges multiple related line charts in a grid to reveal patterns across categorical groupings. A competent speaker would call it a data visualization.

A trellis plot IS a specific kind of faceted visualization: it creates multiple coordinated views (facets) of the same data arranged in a grid. The trellis is the grid arrangement; faceted is the more general concept of multiple coordinated views. A competent speaker classifies a trellis as a type of faceted visualization.

A stacked bar chart IS a specific kind of bar chart: it uses the same basic bar encoding but subdivides each bar into compositional segments. A competent speaker would call a stacked bar chart 'a bar chart.' The INSTANCE_OF direction is correct: specific (stacked bar chart) → general (bar chart). Direction pinned per Law 11d: 'stacked bar chart' as a compositional bar chart variant.
A dot density map IS a specific kind of data visualization — it uses dot density to encode quantitative data spatially. Competent speakers call it 'a visualization.'
Parallel coordinates IS a specific kind of data visualization — multiple vertical axes with lines connecting values. Competent speakers call it 'a chart' or 'a visualization.'
A treatise IS a specific kind of writing — a formal, systematic discourse on a subject. Competent speakers call it 'a treatise' (a form of writing).
A codicil IS a specific kind of writing — an addition or supplement to a document (like a will). Competent speakers call it 'a codicil' (a form of written instrument).
A hexbin plot IS a specific kind of data visualization that bins 2D data into colored hexagonal cells. Competent speakers would call it 'a data visualization.' Direction: specific→general.
A ridge plot (joy plot) IS a specific kind of data visualization that displays density curves across categories. Competent speakers call it 'a visualization.' Direction: specific→general.
A swarm plot IS a specific kind of data visualization — scatter plot with jittering to avoid overlap. Competent speakers call it 'a visualization.' Direction: specific→general.
A Q-Q plot IS a specific kind of data visualization — plots quantiles against each other to compare distributions. Competent speakers call it 'a plot/visualization.' Direction: specific→general.

A stacked bar chart IS a specific kind of data visualization that represents proportional parts of a whole as subdivided bars. Competent speakers call it 'a visualization.' Direction: specific→general.

Sunburst chart IS a specific kind of data visualization — displays hierarchical data using concentric circles. A competent speaker would call it 'a data visualization.' Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

A ladder is a hierarchical structure whose designed purpose is to serve classification — organizing entities into ordered categories. For whose sake? The ladder serves classification. Law 8d: servant→master, not dependency.
A boot IS a specific kind of footwear — encloses the foot and extends above the ankle. A competent speaker would call a boot 'a type of footwear.' Law 9: specific→general.

gantt chart IS a specific kind of data visualization (specific→general per Law 9). Epoch check: data visualization (0.04) is as old or older than gantt chart (0.04), consistent with the general predating the specific.
A hexbin plot IS a specific kind of diagram that visualizes 2D density — specific→general per Law 9. A competent speaker would call it 'a type of diagram.'
A swarm plot IS a specific kind of diagram that visualizes categorical scatter — specific→general per Law 9. A competent speaker would call it 'a type of diagram.'
A ladder IS a specific kind of hierarchy — specific→general per Law 9. A competent speaker would call a ladder 'a type of hierarchy.'
A legend IS a specific kind of folklore per Law 9. A competent speaker would call a legend 'a type of folklore.' Direction: specific→general.

Raincloud plot IS a specific kind of data visualization — a composite display combining box plot, violin plot, and raw data points. A competent speaker would call it 'a type of data visualization.' Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

A semi-structured interview IS a specific kind of survey instrument — it uses a guided set of questions with flexibility to probe, making it a type of survey instrument. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

A structured interview IS a specific kind of survey instrument — it uses a fixed set of standardized questions asked in the same order to all participants, making it a type of survey instrument. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

A control group IS a specific kind of experimental design element — it is the baseline comparison group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment. A competent speaker in research methodology would call it a type of experimental design. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

An axiom IS a specific kind of proposition — a proposition accepted as self-evidently true without proof, serving as a starting point for reasoning. A competent speaker would call an axiom 'a type of proposition.' Direction: specific→general per Law 9.
An ontological category IS a specific kind of category — it is a fundamental division of being or existence into kinds (substance, quality, relation, etc.). Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

Explicit (as a communicative mode — clearly stated, not implied) needs communication to operate now: explicitness is a property of meaning-bearing acts within communication. Remove communication and explicitness has no medium to operate in. This is object-level, not meta-level: the concept of explicitness specifically describes how meaning is conveyed in communicative acts.

A legend IS a specific kind of narrative — a traditional story that may contain historical elements but is primarily passed down through cultural transmission, often blending fact and invention. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

An acquittal IS a specific kind of verdict — the verdict that a defendant is not guilty. Direction specific→general per Law 9. A competent speaker would call an acquittal 'a type of verdict' (specifically, a not-guilty verdict).

Due process IS a specific kind of procedure — a legally mandated process ensuring fair treatment. Direction specific→general per Law 9. A competent speaker would call due process 'a type of procedure' (legal procedure).

A ridgeline plot IS a specific kind of data visualization — a technique for displaying multiple distributions as overlaid density curves in a mountain-range layout. Direction: specific→general per Law 9. A competent speaker in statistics or data analysis would call a ridgeline plot 'a type of data visualization'.
A likelihood ratio IS a specific kind of measurement — it measures how much more likely data is under one hypothesis vs another. Direction specific→general per Law 9.
An odds ratio IS a specific kind of measurement — it measures the strength of association between binary variables. Direction specific→general per Law 9.
A likert scale IS a specific kind of assessment — a structured instrument for measuring attitudes via agreement responses. Direction specific→general per Law 9.

A dendrogram IS a specific kind of data visualization — a tree-diagram visualization of hierarchical relationships. The note pins the visualization sense: dendrogram is a specific type of data visualization tool, and a competent speaker would call it 'a data visualization'. Epoch test confirms data visualization (0.04) predates dendrogram (0.99), so the direction is specific→general per Law 9.

A correlogram IS a specific kind of data visualization — a matrix visualization displaying pairwise correlations as a grid of scatter plots or color cells. The note pins the visualization sense; a competent speaker calls it 'a data visualization'. Epoch test: data visualization (0.04) predates correlogram (not yet epoch'd, but clearly a newer statistical viz technique). Direction specific→general per Law 9.

A radial chart IS a specific kind of data visualization. It encodes data in polar coordinates (angular + radial) to create visual representations of cyclical, hierarchical, or multi-variable data. A competent speaker would classify it as a type of data visualization chart.

A dendrogram is a tree-diagram data visualization that operates by encoding hierarchical relationships through graph structure (nodes + edges). Remove the graph concept (vertices connected by edges) and the dendrogram stops functioning as a visualization form — it literally IS a directed graph with a root and branching edges.

A calculator IS a specific kind of apparatus — a purpose-built instrument/device for performing calculations. The 'which-came-first' test: apparatus (general purpose instrument) predates calculator (specific computational device). A competent speaker calls a calculator 'an apparatus' in its broad sense of a tool or device designed for a particular activity.
Tagging IS a specific kind of categorization — organizing items by assigning discrete labels/tags to them. A competent speaker would call tagging 'a categorization method'. INSTANCE_OF test passes.

A bullet chart IS a specific kind of data visualization: a compact bar-based display of a primary measure against comparative ranges. A competent speaker would call a bullet chart a data visualization — it presents quantitative information visually for rapid comprehension.

An indictment IS a specific kind of legal instrument — a formal accusatory document issued by a grand jury or prosecutor. A competent speaker would call an indictment 'a type of legal charge/document'. Direction: specific→general.

A hypothesis IS a specific kind of proposition — a tentative proposition put forward as a starting point for investigation. A competent speaker would call a hypothesis 'a kind of proposition'. Direction: specific→general.
A fallacy IS a specific kind of error — specifically, a flaw in reasoning or argumentation. A competent speaker would call a fallacy 'a type of reasoning error'. Direction: specific→general.

Collation IS a specific kind of synthesis — it assembles scattered pieces of information into coherent order. A competent speaker would call collation 'a kind of synthesis.' The sense is collation as the practice of gathering and ordering fragments, not as physical collation of sheets.

An apograph IS a specific kind of citation — it is a textual reference that points to a source by reproducing or quoting its content, not merely naming it. A competent speaker in manuscript studies would recognize an apograph as 'a type of citation' (specifically, a full-reference citation). Direction: specific→general.

A network graph IS a specific kind of data visualization — it visually encodes relationships as nodes and edges to reveal patterns in connectivity. A competent speaker in data science would call it 'a kind of data visualization.' Direction: specific→general. INSTANCE_OF per Law 9.
An apograph IS a specific kind of manuscript — a handwritten copy of a text that differs from the original in minor ways. Direction specific→general per Law 9.
An indictment IS a specific kind of legal document — a formal accusation filed by a government. Direction specific→general per Law 9.

A legal document needs legal procedure to operate — without the procedure, the document is merely paper with no legal force. Remove legal procedure and legal documents stop functioning as instruments of law.

Summarization IS a specific kind of synthesis — it combines and condenses source material into a coherent shorter form. Both involve combining elements, but summarization is specifically a reduction operation on existing content.

A premise IS a specific kind of proposition — a statement assumed or accepted as true in the context of an argument, from which conclusions are drawn. Direction: specific (argument component) → general (statement claimed as true). Law 9.

Scatter plot IS a specific kind of data visualization — a chart that plots individual data points on Cartesian coordinates. Direction: specific (scatter plot, a visualization technique) → general (data visualization, the category). Per Law 9.

Histogram IS a specific kind of data visualization — a graphical representation of the distribution of numerical data using bins. Direction: specific (histogram, a visualization technique) → general (data visualization, the category). Per Law 9.
A sparkline IS a specific kind of data visualization — a small, high-resolution chart that shows trends in data without axes or labels. Direction: specific visualization → general category per Law 9.
Summarization IS a specific kind of writing — it produces condensed text from source material. Direction: specific writing technique → general writing category per Law 9.
standard error IS a specific kind of estimation method: it estimates the variability of a sample statistic. A competent speaker would call it 'an estimation technique.'
A bell curve IS a specific kind of data visualization: a graphical chart showing a symmetric distribution. Competent speakers classify it as a chart/visualization technique.

Margin of error is mathematically derived from standard error: ME = z* x SE. Standard error existed first and fed into the later development of margin of error concepts. The removal test also holds: without standard error as a concept, the margin of error computation has no basis.

Standard error measures the variability of a sample statistic across repeated samples. Remove sampling as a concept, and standard error has nothing to operate on — it is literally the standard deviation of the sampling distribution. This is a constitutive, present-tense dependency.

stem-and-leaf IS a specific kind of data visualization: it displays data distributions using a tabular layout where values are split into stems and leaves. A competent speaker would call it 'a type of data visualization' or 'a data display method'.

A spreadsheet IS a specific kind of apparatus — a human-made tool that extends the capacity to organize, calculate, and analyze data in a grid format. A competent speaker calls it 'a tool for organizing data.' INSTANCE_OF direction: specific (spreadsheet) → general (apparatus). The removal test also passes: remove apparatus as a concept and spreadsheet loses its categorization as a tool-class, though it still OPERATES — but INSTANCE_OF only asks 'is X a kind of Y?' which this clearly satisfies.

A correlation coefficient IS a specific kind of correlation — it quantifies the degree and direction of a relationship between two variables. Direction: specific (correlation coefficient) → general (correlation). Law 9.
A legal procedure IS a specific kind of procedure — a formally established method within the legal domain. Direction: specific (legal procedure) → general (procedure). Law 9.

burden-of-proof is a principle that only operates within legal procedure — it defines who must prove what in a legal process. Remove legal procedure and burden-of-proof has no domain to operate in. Direction: burden-of-proof (newer, 0.73) → legal procedure (older, 0.27). Constitutive present-tense dependency per Law 8.

spreadsheet is a software application paradigm for structured data manipulation and calculation. Remove software as a construct and spreadsheet ceases to operate — it cannot function outside the software paradigm. Direction: spreadsheet (newer, 0.47) → software (older, 0.27). Constitutive dependency per Law 8.

A corollary IS a specific kind of proposition — one that follows readily from a proposition already proven or established. Direction: specific→general. Precheck clear: no corollary↔proposition edge exists.
A presumption IS a specific kind of assumption — one that is accepted as true without proof, often as a starting point for reasoning. Direction: specific→general.

A spreadsheet is a specific kind of data visualization — a structured visual format for displaying quantitative data in rows and columns, making patterns and relationships immediately visible. A competent speaker would call a spreadsheet 'a kind of data visualization.' Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

A funnel chart is a specific kind of data visualization — a visual display showing quantities at successive process stages through narrowing segments. A competent speaker calls it 'a kind of data visualization.' Direction: specific→general per Law 9.
A sampling frame IS a specific kind of statistical construct — an enumerated list of elements from which a sample is drawn, central to survey statistics. Direction: specific→general.
A confounder IS a specific kind of statistical concept — a variable that distorts the apparent relationship between exposure and outcome. Direction: specific→general.

Discovery operates only within the framework of legal procedure — remove the rules of civil procedure governing discovery, and the process of compelled disclosure of evidence ceases to function. This is a present-tense dependency (Law 8), not historical.

A synopsis IS a specific kind of abstract. Both are condensed summaries of longer works stating purpose and content. A synopsis extends to narrative/creative works while abstract is scholarly — but both share the same structural purpose: condensed summary for quick assessment. A competent speaker calls a synopsis 'a kind of summary/abstract.' Direction: specific→general.

A funnel chart visualizes quantities at successive process stages. Remove the concept of process and the chart type ceases to operate — the removal test passes. A funnel chart without process stages is just colored blocks with no meaning.

Begging-the-question (petitio principii) IS a specific kind of logical fallacy — an argument whose conclusion is assumed in its premises. A competent speaker calls it 'a fallacy.' Direction specific→general.
Burden-of-proof is a specific kind of principle — the rule assigning who must establish a proposition. Applies across law, science, debate. Direction: specific→general.

A standard of proof IS a specific kind of principle — the rule specifying the required level of evidence (beyond reasonable doubt, preponderance, clear and convincing). Direction: specific→general. Note pins principle as a governing rule, not a vague norm.

A sampling frame is the concrete list or source from which a sample is drawn. It only operates within the context of statistical sampling. Remove statistical sampling (statistics) and the sampling frame concept ceases to operate — it is not a standalone concept. Present-tense dependency, not just historical.

Statistics operates through mathematical operations — probability theory, inferential formulas, and computational methods are constitutive to its function. Remove mathematics and statistics cannot compute, infer, or operate at all. This passes the removal test: statistics stops working without its mathematical foundation.

Precommitment IS a specific kind of strategy — a method of deliberately binding one's future self to a course of action to overcome present-bias. Direction: specific→general. Note pins strategy as a deliberate plan of action; precommitment is a subtype focused on self-binding across time.

Removal test: remove legal procedure and standard of proof ceases to operate — it specifies the evidence threshold within an active procedure. Without procedure, the concept has no working context. Law 8 passes.

Removal test: remove the concept of self and precommitment ceases to operate — it binds one's future self to a present decision. Without the self as a temporal entity, there is nothing to bind. The concept dissolves, not merely becomes unsayable. Law 8 passes.

Skepticism IS a specific kind of strategy — the deliberate method of doubting claims and seeking evidence before accepting them. Direction: specific→general. A competent speaker would call skepticism 'a strategy' of inquiry.

Information design arranges visual and structural signs (icons, typography, layout hierarchies) to make information comprehensible. Remove symbols — signs that stand for something else — and information design has no material to work with: there is no sign-based representation to design. The removal test passes under Law 8.

Data visualization IS a specific kind of information design — it is the application of information design principles (visual encoding, hierarchy, layout, legibility) specifically to numerical and tabular data. A competent speaker would call data visualization a form of information design. Direction: specific→general under Law 9.

Synopsis IS a specific kind of summary — a brief statement of the main points of a larger work. Both condense information, but a synopsis preserves the argument structure while a summary may be more general. Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

An abridgment IS a specific kind of summary — a shortened version of a written work that preserves key content. While abridgment focuses on textual reduction, it is still fundamentally a condensed form of the original, making it a type of summary. Direction: specific→general.

A pre-mortem IS a specific kind of summary — it summarizes projected future failures and their causes before a project begins. It condenses anticipated outcomes into a structured overview. Direction: specific→general.

Rationalization derives from cognitive dissonance — it is the self-justifying narrative constructed to resolve the psychological tension of holding conflicting beliefs. The dissonance came first; rationalization is the response mechanism.

Skepticism operates by doubting claims and seeking evidence. Remove doubt — the capacity to withhold assent from claims — and skepticism has no operating mechanism. The removal test passes: without doubt, skepticism cannot function.

Cognitive dissonance requires holding conflicting beliefs to generate tension. Remove belief — the mental acceptance of propositions as true — and there is nothing to be dissonant about. The removal test passes: without beliefs, cognitive dissonance cannot operate.

Self-deception requires holding a false belief while simultaneously being aware of contradictory evidence. Remove belief — the acceptance of propositions as true — and self-deception cannot operate: there is nothing to be falsely believed. Removal test passes.

Self-deception IS a specific kind of deception — one where the deceiver and the deceived are the same person. Direction: specific→general. A competent speaker would call self-deception a form of deception.

A nudge is a behavioral intervention designed to counter anchoring bias. Remove anchoring and a nudge targeting it stops operating — the bias is its operational target. Direction: nudge (newer, 0.46) → anchoring (older, 0.38).

A nudge is a behavioral intervention designed to counter confirmation bias. Remove confirmation bias and a nudge targeting it stops operating — the bias is its operational target. Direction: nudge (newer, 0.46) → confirmation-bias (older, 0.38).

Self-deception requires holding multiple perspectives on one's own beliefs — a meta-cognitive capacity. Without the ability to model one's own mental states (meta-cognition), self-deception as a phenomenon cannot arise. Direction: self-deception (newer, 0.99) → meta-cognition (older, 0.04).

A nudge is a behavioral intervention designed for the sake of countering anchoring bias. Law 8d: X exists to serve Y means SERVES. Nudge's purpose is to further anchoring's mitigation — the servant (nudge) points at the master (anchoring). Remove anchoring and the nudge's purpose vanishes, but nudge as a concept survives, so this is teleological, not constitutive.

A nudge targets confirmation bias by design. Law 8d: nudge's purpose is to counter confirmation bias, so nudge SERVES confirmation-bias (servant→master). Law 8c: purpose is not dependency. This is teleological, not constitutive.

Misinformation exploits cognitive biases including anchoring in its persuasive effect. The removal test: remove anchoring from the cognitive landscape and misinformation's persuasive mechanism loses a key lever — it still operates via other biases, but anchoring is a fundamental mechanism misinformation depends on for its persuasive power.

Misinformation's persuasive mechanism depends on confirmation bias: people accept information that confirms pre-existing beliefs. The removal test — remove confirmation bias and misinformation loses its primary vector of acceptance through motivated reasoning. Misinformation may still reach some people, but its core persuasive mechanism depends on the cognitive tendency to favor confirmatory evidence.

socks requires the concept of clothing to exist: socks are a specific type of foot covering within the category of clothing. Removal test — remove the concept of clothing, and socks lose their entire categorical framework. The item itself is a garment; garments only exist within the clothing construct. Direction confirmed by edge-test: clothing epoch 0.23, socks epoch 0.31 — clothing came first.

garden hoe and garden-hoe are naming variants of the same construct. garden-hoe was established as the canonical form (normalized name per Law 12). The variant 'garden hoe' depends on the canonical form for its identity — they refer to the same object, and the variant form is only meaningful relative to the established canonical entry.

Law 8 removal test: remove belief (the mechanism of accepting information as true) — misinformation stops operating. Misinformation's mode of action is: false info presented → accepted as true (belief formed) → acted upon. Without belief, the info remains unaccepted data; the misinformation mechanism collapses. This is object-level: about how the social phenomenon operates, not about naming it (Law 2b).

A laptop IS a specific kind of tool — an artifact that extends human computation and communication capacity. Law 9: specific→general. Law 11c: tool carries its broad sense as any artifact extending human capacity, including passive artifacts.

Self-deception operates through confirmation bias — the mechanism of selective attention to confirming evidence and dismissal of disconfirming evidence. Remove confirmation bias and self-deception loses its primary cognitive mechanism; it can no longer filter evidence systematically.

Anchoring works because the subject believes (accepts as plausible) the initial value presented. Remove belief as a capacity and anchoring has no psychological substrate to operate on; the anchor cannot take hold.

Belief bias is the tendency to accept belief-congruent conclusions regardless of logical validity. It requires belief as its substrate — remove belief and belief bias has nothing to bias toward or against.
black-swan IS a specific kind of heuristic: it is a cognitive shortcut for reasoning about low-probability, high-impact events. Nearest kind is heuristic (Law 9, Law 11e).

Anchoring (and adjustment) is a specific kind of cognitive heuristic identified by Kahneman and Tversky. The filer's pinned sense: anchoring IS a heuristic — a mental shortcut where initial values serve as reference points in judgment. Nearest kind is heuristic (Law 9).

Remove memory and anchoring stops operating: the anchoring effect requires remembering the initial anchor value and adjusting from it. Without memory, no anchor reference exists. Law 8 removal test passes.

Anchoring needs information to operate: the bias functions through exposure to an initial value (the anchor) that influences subsequent judgment. Remove information and anchoring cannot occur no anchor value exists to exert influence. Law 8 removal test passes. Object-level dependency not meta-level.

Confirmation bias needs information to operate: the tendency to seek interpret and recall information in a way that confirms preexisting beliefs requires information to process. Remove information and confirmation bias cannot operate. Law 8 removal test passes.

Chart is a specific kind of data visualization (Law 9). A competent speaker would call a chart a type of data visualization — it encodes data into visual form. Files against the nearest kind; no intervening rung on the INSTANCE_OF ladder.

An executive summary is a specific kind of summary — one tailored for executive decision-makers, focusing on key findings and conclusions rather than methodological detail. A competent speaker would call an executive summary a type of summary. Files against the nearest kind per Law 9.

Anchoring needs belief to operate now (Law 8): the bias functions by using an initial value as a reference point that shapes subsequent belief-formation and judgment. Remove belief — the capacity to hold and adjust beliefs — and anchoring stops operating entirely. The anchor only influences through the mechanism of belief revision.

Confirmation bias needs belief to operate now (Law 8): the tendency to seek, interpret, and recall information in ways that confirm preexisting beliefs requires beliefs to exist first. Remove belief — the capacity to hold preexisting positions — and confirmation bias cannot operate. The bias is defined by its relationship to belief, not merely by information-processing.

A chart IS a specific kind of data visualization — it encodes data into a structured visual form. A competent speaker would call a chart a type of data visualization. Specific→general INSTANCE_OF to nearest kind.

debiasing needs cognitive-bias to operate now: debiasing techniques (reflective thinking, structured analysis, perspective-taking) are designed to counteract systematic errors in reasoning. Remove cognitive-bias — there is nothing to debias, and the practice ceases to operate. The removal test passes at the object level (Law 8b): debiasing's mechanism targets cognitive-bias-specific patterns, not just any error.

Debasing IS a specific kind of cognitive strategy — a method designed to reduce or eliminate systematic errors in thinking. Specific→general per Law 9. Nearest kind is cognitive-strategy, not cognitive-bias (Law 8c: identity/purpose is not dependency).

A nudge IS a specific kind of intervention — a subtle change in the choice architecture that influences behavior without forbidding options. Specific→general per Law 9. A competent speaker would call a nudge 'an intervention.'

Removal test: remove metacognition — does debiasing stop operating? Yes. Debiasing requires awareness of one's own thinking processes to detect and correct errors. Without metacognition (thinking about thinking), there is no mechanism to detect bias or apply correction. Operation, not sayability: debiasing techniques require metacognitive monitoring to function.

Removal test: remove intention — does provocation stop operating? Yes. Provocation is defined by its intent to elicit a reaction; without intentional provoking, there is only accidental triggering. Direction: provocation (specific concept) DEPENDS_ON intention (general cognitive state). The dependency is constitutive — the concept's operation requires the agent to have the purpose of eliciting a response.

Removal test: remove evaluation — does curating stop operating? Yes. Curating is the selective organization of items based on judged quality or relevance. Without evaluation (the act of assessing value, relevance, or merit), there is no curation — only accumulation or random ordering.

Removal test: remove uncertainty — does black-swan stop operating? Yes. A black swan is defined by its unpredictability — the gap between what we think we know and what actually happens. Without uncertainty (epistemic limitation), the concept of an unexpected, high-impact event collapses. The removal of uncertainty means all outcomes are known, and 'black swan' has no meaning.

Removal test: remove comparison — does decoy-effect stop operating? Yes. The decoy effect operates by making one option look more attractive through comparison with a dominated decoy option. Without the mechanism of comparison between options, the decoy has no effect. The phenomenon is entirely defined by how comparison shifts preference.

Status-quo bias IS a specific kind of cognitive-bias — a systematic preference for the current state. Specific→general per Law 9. Epoch test: status-quo-bias (0.01) is newer than cognitive-bias (0.35).

Removal test: remove satisficing and bounded rationality stops operating — bounded rationality is a model that describes satisficing behavior. Without the concept of selecting threshold-satisfactory options, the model has no content. Direction: bounded rationality needs satisficing to operate.

satisficing IS a specific kind of heuristic: a decision shortcut that selects the first acceptable option rather than optimizing. Satisficing maps to 'a heuristic' per competent speaker usage. Specific→general per Law 9.

The concept of anchoring-bias depends on the concept of anchoring: without the concept of an anchor (initial reference point that disproportionately influences decisions), the concept of anchoring-bias (the tendency to over-rely on such anchors) cannot operate. Removal test: remove anchoring and anchoring-bias loses its entire referent — it stops operating, not just being sayable. Law 8.

anchoring-bias IS a specific kind of heuristic — a competent speaker would call an anchoring bias 'a heuristic.' It is a cognitive shortcut that produces predictable errors. Specific→general per Law 9, against the nearest kind (heuristic). Anchoring-bias is not a kind of bias broadly, but a specific heuristic type.

Bounded rationality is a framework developed within (and made coherent by) the heuristics-and-biases research program — remove that program and bounded rationality loses its operational context and becomes an empty claim.

Decision fatigue is a specific phenomenon where decision quality deteriorates after prolonged choice, falling under the broader framework of bounded rationality (limits to human decision-making). INSTANCE_OF direction: specific phenomenon → general category. Removal test confirms: decision fatigue IS a kind of bounded rationality — a concrete manifestation of how human rationality is constrained.

Metonymy is a specific kind of figure of speech where a thing is referred to by the name of something closely associated with it (e.g. 'the White House' for the US administration). Per Law 9: a competent speaker would call metonymy 'a figure of speech.' Pinned sense: figure-of-speech as defined in its accepted definition — a rhetorical device that departs from literal meaning.

Bounded rationality is a framework modeling limits in human decision-making due to cognitive constraints — memory is a core constraint. Remove memory (cognitive capacity for encoding/retrieval) and the entire formal structure of bounded rationality collapses: it has no operational target since it models how limited memory and information processing produce satisficing rather than optimizing. Object-level dependency, not meta-level — the removal test asks about the framework's operation, not its sayability.

Anchoring bias operates by causing an initial value (the anchor) to be incorporated into subsequent judgments and decisions. This requires the subject to hold a belief in or adjustment toward the anchor value. Remove anchoring's reliance on belief in the anchor and the bias stops operating.

Choice-overload IS a specific kind of bounded rationality: it describes how excess options degrade decision quality, representing a concrete limit on rational choice under abundance. A competent speaker would call choice-overload 'a form of bounded rationality.' Direction: specific→general. Nearest kind check: bounded rationality is the established framework for limits to rational decision-making.

Synecdoche is a specific kind of metonymy where the associative relation is specifically part-whole (or whole-part). Per Law 9, a competent speaker would call synecdoche a type of metonymy — specific→general INSTANCE_OF.

Elaborative interrogation requires metacognitive operation — the technique generates 'why' questions to connect new info to prior knowledge, which demands awareness of one's own thinking. Remove metacognition and this learning technique cannot function.

Loss aversion is a specific kind of cognitive bias: the tendency to prefer avoiding losses over acquiring equivalent gains. Law 9 — a competent speaker calls loss aversion 'a cognitive bias.' Specific→general INSTANCE_OF.

Negativity bias requires memory to operate — the bias emerges from comparing the valence and recall strength of negative versus positive experiences. Remove memory and there is no capacity to retain, retrieve, or weigh differential valences.

Law 8 removal test: remove choice and choice-overload ceases to operate entirely. The phenomenon of being overwhelmed by options requires choices to exist. Remove Y and X stops working — not just sayable.

Law 9: anchoring-bias is a specific kind of bounded rationality phenomenon — the tendency to rely too heavily on the first piece of information encountered. Within bounded rationality's framework, anchoring is a canonical way human judgment deviates from rational optimization. Specific-to-general INSTANCE_OF.
Law 9: scarcity-mindset IS a specific kind of cognitive-bias — the systematic distortion in judgment that arises from perceived resource insufficiency. Direction specific→general correct.
Law 9: heuristics-and-biases IS a specific kind of bounded rationality — the systematic deviations from rationality that arise from mental shortcuts. Direction specific→general correct.

optimism-bias requires heuristic processing to operate: it is a systematic overestimation of positive outcomes produced by cognitive shortcuts. Remove heuristics — mental shortcuts and heuristic processing — and optimism-bias ceases to function. Removal test passes: without the heuristic mechanism, the bias has no operational pathway.

anchoring-bias IS a specific kind of heuristics-and-biases phenomenon: the tendency to rely too heavily on initial information. A competent speaker would classify anchoring as a heuristic-and-bias. Direction specific→general.

confirmation-bias IS a specific kind of heuristics-and-biases phenomenon: the tendency to search for, interpret, and recall information that confirms preexisting beliefs. A competent speaker would classify confirmation-bias as a heuristic-and-bias. Direction specific→general.

availability-bias IS a specific kind of heuristics-and-biases phenomenon: the tendency to overestimate the importance of information that is readily available. A competent speaker would classify it as a heuristic-and-bias. Direction specific→general.

Law 8 removal test: working memory requires attention to encode, maintain, and manipulate information. Remove attention and working memory stops operating — it cannot hold or update representations without attentional focus. This is a real operational dependency, not a meta-level 'both are concepts' relationship.

Law 8 removal test: scarcity mindset is a cognitive state that captures and narrows attention. Remove attention and the bias has nothing to narrow — it cannot operate. The entire mechanism of attentional tunneling under scarcity requires attention to exist as a target. This is an operational dependency, not a meta-level relationship.

anchoring-bias DEPENDS_ON heuristic passes the Law 8 removal test. The anchoring effect operates through heuristic processing — the anchoring-and-adjustment heuristic. Remove heuristic processing and anchoring cannot operate: there would be no mental shortcut to anchor on, and no heuristic-driven adjustment process to produce the bias. This is constitutive: anchoring is a phenomenon produced by heuristics, and removing heuristics removes anchoring's mechanism.

bounded rationality DEPENDS_ON decision passes the Law 8 removal test. Bounded rationality is a theory/framework for understanding how actual decisions are made under constraints. Remove decision as a subject and bounded rationality has nothing to operate upon — the concept's entire domain is the study of decision processes. This is constitutive: bounded rationality exists to explain decision-making, and without decisions the concept has no operation.

Scarcity mindset operates by occupying working memory resources (the 'tunneling' effect). Remove working memory and the scarcity mindset has no cognitive mechanism to hijack — it cannot operate. The removal test passes: scarcity's cognitive impact depends on working memory being available to be narrowed.

Information overload occurs when input exceeds available attentional capacity. Remove attention and there is no mechanism for overload — the concept cannot arise. The removal test passes: information overload depends on attention being finite and in use.

A decision cascade is a chain of dependent decisions where each decision triggers the next. Remove decision and the cascade has nothing to cascade. The removal test passes: decision-cascade depends on the operation of individual decisions.

Cognitive depletion is a state of exhausted mental resources that depends on cognitive load (the demand placed on those resources) to operate. Removal test: remove cognitive load and cognitive depletion has no demand to deplete — the state ceases to operate.
Decision requires memory to operate: removing memory eliminates the capacity to recall information needed for any choice. The removal test passes — without memory, decision cannot function.

Recency-bias is a specific kind of cognitive-bias: the tendency to weigh recent experiences more heavily than earlier ones. Law 9: 'X is a specific kind of Y' = INSTANCE_OF. Pinned sense: recency-bias as a systematic error pattern in memory retrieval, a recognized subtype of cognitive bias.

Friction is a human-made concept describing resistance in physical, social, or systemic contexts. Law 9: friction IS a kind of concept — specifically, a concept for resistance. Pinned sense: friction as an abstract concept/model for resistance across domains, not the physical phenomenon itself.

removal test: remove memory and the optimism-bias mechanism ceases to operate — the bias is a systematic weighting of remembered outcomes toward positive expectations, and that weighting requires memory traces to function. Epoch test confirms memory (0.27) predates optimism-bias (0.38). Object-level dependency on the cognitive mechanism, not meta-level sayability.

removal test: remove memory and the cognitive-depletion model ceases to operate — the model describes exhausted mental resources, and resources are stored/retrieved via memory. Epoch test confirms memory (0.27) predates cognitive-depletion (1.01). Object-level dependency on the cognitive mechanism.

Inattentional-blindness is a specific kind of cognitive-bias: the failure to detect a salient stimulus when attention is engaged elsewhere. Law 9: X is a specific kind of Y = INSTANCE_OF. The filer pins inattentional-blindness as a systematic perceptual error, squarely within cognitive-bias.

Removal test: inattentional-blindness is the failure to detect a salient stimulus when attention is engaged elsewhere. Remove attention and the phenomenon has no cognitive mechanism to operate — it is fundamentally about attentional capture. The which-came-first test confirms attention predates the conceptualization.

Removal test: information-overload occurs when the volume of available information exceeds attentional capacity. Remove attention and the overload mechanism cannot operate — there is no capacity to overwhelm. Information and attention are both required; attention is the limiting resource.
hyperbole IS a specific kind of figure of speech — extreme exaggeration used for emphasis or effect. A competent speaker would call hyperbole 'a figure of speech' (Law 9).

Removal test: inattentional-blindness occurs when attention is consumed by executive allocation (focusing on one task while another is present). Remove executive-function (the capacity to direct and regulate attention) and the phenomenon has no mechanism — you can't be 'blind to what you weren't attending to' without the executive mechanism that allocates attention in the first place. Constitutive, not incidental.

Removal test: information-overload occurs when available information exceeds processing capacity. That capacity IS executive-function — the ability to direct attention, filter, evaluate, and process information. Remove executive-function and there is no capacity that can be exceeded; the overload mechanism cannot operate. Constitutive dependency.
Conceptual metaphor IS a specific kind of theory from cognitive linguistics proposing abstract concepts are understood through systematic mapping from concrete domains.

Removal test: executive-function operates by directing and regulating attentional resources. Remove attention and executive-function has nothing to direct — it stops operating entirely. Attention is the prerequisite capacity that executive-function acts upon.
