No. Hazard-assessment evaluates hazards, but it needs real-world data about what conditions exist, what near-misses occurred, what unsafe acts were observed. Safety-observation provides that data. Without it, hazard-assessment has no input and stops operating.

Safety-training is maintained for the sake of risk-management: it builds worker knowledge and safe-behavior capacity so that risks are identified and managed proactively. Law 8d: servant(safety-training)→master(risk-management).
Safety-training is maintained for the sake of hazard-mitigation: it equips workers with the skills and awareness needed to implement mitigation controls in daily practice. Law 8d: servant→master.

Safety-signage is maintained for the sake of hazard-mitigation: visual indicators are engineered controls that mitigate hazards by warning of dangers and directing safe behavior. Law 8d: servant→master.

Hazard-mitigation is maintained for the sake of risk-management. It implements the concrete strategies and controls that risk-management prescribes — removing mitigation would leave risk-management with no operational means to reduce hazards.
Safety-metric is maintained for the sake of hazard-assessment. Quantitative measures of safety performance provide the data that hazard-assessment uses to evaluate risk levels and track improvements.

Safety-reporting collects and communicates safety data (incidents, near-misses, observations) that hazard-assessment uses to evaluate risk levels and identify patterns. Law 8d: servant(safety-reporting)→master(hazard-assessment). Reporting is maintained so hazard-assessment has timely, comprehensive data to work with.

Safety-reporting surfaces incident and near-miss data that hazard-mitigation uses to prioritize and target interventions. Law 8d: servant(safety-reporting)→master(hazard-mitigation). Reporting is maintained so that mitigation strategies are informed by actual events and trends.

An opinion IS a kind of belief. It is a belief held with explicit acknowledgment of uncertainty — the holder recognizes it could be wrong. Law 9: a competent speaker would call an opinion 'a belief' (specifically, a tentative one). Nearest kind: belief, not judgment (which requires reasoning) or view (which is more subjective).

A sensitivity analysis IS a kind of analysis. It is a specific analytical method that determines how different values of an independent variable affect a dependent variable under a given set of assumptions. Law 9: a competent speaker would call a sensitivity analysis 'an analysis.' Nearest kind: analysis.
donut chart IS a specific kind of pie chart per Law 9: specific→general. A donut chart is a pie chart with the center removed.

safety-observation SERVES hazard-assessment per Law 8d: servant→master. Systematic observation of safety conditions provides data that hazard-assessment uses to evaluate risk levels and identify patterns.

layer-of-protection is built on top of hazard-assessment practice: you must assess hazards before designing layered safeguards. which-came-first test confirms hazard-assessment (epoch 0.08) predates layer-of-protection (epoch 1.01).

layer-of-protection is built and maintained for the sake of risk-management: its designed purpose is to manage multiple independent risk layers so that no single point of failure defeats the whole system. Servant (layer-of-protection) points at master (risk-management), per Law 8d.

layer-of-protection derives from the older, more general principle of fault-tolerance. which-came-first confirms fault-tolerance (epoch 0) predates layer-of-protection (epoch 1.01). The practice of arranging independent safeguards builds directly on the earlier concept of designing systems to tolerate component failures.

Safety-training exists to ensure personnel understand and correctly maintain layered safeguards; trained staff operate and sustain the full protection hierarchy, making layer-of-protection functional in practice.

Root-cause-analysis is a specific form of hazard assessment: it systematically investigates incidents to identify underlying causal factors, making it a concrete method within the broader hazard-assessment practice.

Bow-tie-analysis is a specific hazard-assessment technique that visualizes threats, controls, and consequences in a bow-tie diagram. It is a concrete method within the broader hazard-assessment practice.

Safety-management is the organizational framework maintained for the sake of risk-management: it systematises hazard identification, risk assessment, and control implementation as the operational mechanism by which risk-management functions.

Remove hazard-assessment (the practice of systematically identifying and evaluating hazards) and safety-management stops operating — its core function is the systematisation of hazard identification and risk assessment. Present-tense dependency confirmed by the removal test.

Safety-management is maintained for the sake of hazard-mitigation: it systematises the identification, assessment, and implementation of controls that directly mitigate hazards. Its designed purpose is to advance hazard-mitigation outcomes.

Job-safety-analysis is a task-level hazard identification method designed and maintained within safety-management's framework. Its purpose is to feed structured hazard data into safety-management's cycle. SERVES: the method (JSA) points at the system it serves (safety-management).

Hierarchy-of-controls is a method for ranking and selecting control measures, deployed and maintained within safety-management's framework. Its designed purpose is to advance safety-management's ability to implement effective controls. SERVES: the ranking method (hierarchy) points at the system it serves (safety-management).

Safety-inspection serves safety-management: the inspection practice feeds structured condition reports and compliance data into the safety-management framework, enabling it to systematise hazard identification and corrective action tracking. SERVES direction correct — inspection is the servant, safety-management the master. Law 8d satisfied.

safety-case is a specific structured argument that a system's risks are adequately controlled, used to support go/no-go decisions. It is a specific kind of hazard-assessment method. Precheck: safety-case is ACCEPTED, hazard-assessment is ACCEPTED.
risk-management is the older, more foundational practice; risk-treatment (selecting/implementing risk options) evolved from it. Epoch test confirms risk-management predates risk-treatment.
incident reports provide empirical evidence of hazards and near-misses that feed into safety-case documentation. Per Law 8d: for whose sake? incident reports serve the safety-case's evidence base.

Toolbox talks are short, focused safety briefings conducted for the sake of safety-training. Their designed purpose is to deliver safety knowledge to workers at the point of work, making them a delivery method for safety-training.

Behavioral safety programs are designed for the sake of risk-management. Their purpose is to observe, coach, and modify worker behaviors to reduce the likelihood of incidents — a risk-reduction strategy within the broader risk-management framework.

Hazard identification exists for the sake of hazard-analysis. You identify hazards first so you can analyze them — the identification step serves the analytical step. Per Law 8d: the designed purpose of identifying hazards is to feed the analysis process.

Safety audits are conducted for the sake of compliance. Their designed purpose is to verify that an organization meets applicable safety standards, regulations, and requirements — making compliance the master that safety-audit serves.

FMEA is a systematic, structured method for identifying potential failure modes and their effects. It is a specific instance of the broader hazard-assessment practice. Law 9: FMEA is a specific kind of hazard assessment method.

Behavioral-safety programs are designed and maintained for the sake of building and reinforcing safety-culture. Their purpose is to shift organizational attitudes and norms around safety by making safety behaviors visible, observable, and socially reinforced. The servant (behavioral-safety) points at the master (safety-culture).

Intellectual-humility — the disposition to recognize the limits of one's knowledge and remain open to revision — is cultivated for the sake of scientific-method. It ensures researchers weigh evidence fairly, update beliefs when contradicted, and resist confirmation bias. The designed purpose of intellectual humility in epistemic practice is to sustain the integrity of the scientific method.

Incident reports are built and maintained for the sake of risk-management. Their purpose is to capture information about incidents so risks can be assessed, tracked, and mitigated. Law 8d: for-whose-sake arrow, servant→master.

lockout-tagout is a specific hazard-mitigation method: it is a structured procedure that physically isolates energy sources to prevent unexpected startup during maintenance — a concrete instance of the broader hazard-mitigation practice.

hierarchy-of-controls is a specific hazard-mitigation framework: it ranks mitigation strategies from most to least effective (elimination, substitution, engineering, administrative, PPE). It is a systematic approach within the broader practice of hazard-mitigation.

Safety-observation gathers frontline safety data (near misses, unsafe conditions) which feeds into safety-governance decision-making. Purpose-directed: observations exist to inform governance, not the reverse.

Control-measures are physical or procedural safeguards implemented for the sake of risk-management: they exist to reduce or eliminate risks identified during hazard analysis. Purpose-directed — the servant (control) points at the master (risk-management), Law 8d.

Safety-audit generates systematic findings and reports that feed into safety-communication channels. The audit's purpose includes producing communicated information — the servant (safety-audit) points at the master (safety-communication).

Safety-training is a mechanism through which safety-governance policies are implemented and disseminated. Training exists to put governance into practice — the servant (training) points at the master (governance). Law 8d.

Emergency-response exists to implement safety-governance policies in practice. Law 8d: servant (emergency-response)→master (safety-governance). The purpose of emergency response is to fulfill governance — it is the operational arm through which governance becomes effective during incidents.

Remove safety-communication channels — and emergency response cannot operate: it cannot alert, coordinate, or direct. Law 8's removal test: X stops OPERATING when Y is removed. Communication is operationally necessary for emergency response, not just conceptually necessary. This is present-tense operational dependency, not meta-level.

Safety-communication is the practice of conveying risk-related information, alerts, and assessments. It is built and maintained for the sake of risk-management: communication enables risk managers to identify, evaluate, and act on risk data. Law 8d: servant (safety-communication) → master (risk-management).

Emergency-response is the operational practice of responding to incidents and hazards. It exists for the sake of risk-management: emergency response is risk management's reactive arm — implementing controls when prevention fails. Law 8d: servant (emergency-response) → master (risk-management).

Law 8d: control measures are implemented for the sake of safety management. Their designed purpose is to fulfill safety management's objective of reducing risk to acceptable levels. The servant (control measure) points at the master (safety management).

management-review is the practice where organizational leaders assess management system effectiveness, conformance, and suitability. It is built and maintained for the sake of safety-governance — to ensure oversight, accountability, and strategic direction of safety practices. SERVES test (Law 8d): remove safety-governance and management-review loses its purpose and reason to exist. The arrow: servant(management-review) → master(safety-governance).

safety-climate IS built and maintained for the sake of safety-management. The measurement of collective attitudes about safety provides data that safety-management uses to assess system effectiveness and guide corrective action. Teleology: safety-climate (servant) → safety-management (master). Law 8d.

management-review IS maintained for the sake of safety-management. Top-leadership evaluation of the management system's suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness exists to improve the safety-management system's operation. Servant: management-review → master: safety-management. Law 8d.

near-miss-reporting IS built and maintained for the sake of hazard-assessment: reporting near misses produces data that hazard-assessment uses to identify systemic weaknesses before incidents occur. The purpose is by design — near-miss programs are instrumented specifically to feed hazard assessment processes.

safety-climate IS maintained for the sake of hazard-assessment: measuring collective safety attitudes surfaces systemic organizational factors (norms, communication, resource perception) that contribute to hazard creation. Safety climate data feeds into hazard assessment to identify root organizational causes. Purpose is by design.

Near-miss-reporting is a specific practice within the general category of hazard-assessment: it systematically collects and analyzes information about close calls to identify potential hazards before they materialize. A competent speaker would call near-miss-reporting 'a kind of hazard-assessment'.

Technical-debt is a specific kind of debt: the implied cost of additional rework caused by choosing an easy (limited) solution now instead of using a better approach that would take longer. The specific→general relation: technical-debt IS a particular domain of debt (engineering/software).

Safety-margin IS maintained for the sake of risk-management: it provides a built-in buffer that ensures the system operates within safe bounds even under uncertainty. The purpose is by design — safety-margins are deliberate risk-control mechanisms within the broader risk-management system.

Parsimony IS a specific criterion: the principle that among competing hypotheses, the one with the fewest assumptions should be selected. It is a criterion used in scientific reasoning and model selection.

Safety-observability is built and maintained for the sake of hazard-assessment: it provides the continuous monitoring, dashboards, and alerts that feed into identifying and evaluating hazards. The servant (observability) points at the master (hazard-assessment) — Law 8d.

Safety-investment is built and maintained for the sake of risk-management: it allocates resources, budget, and infrastructure specifically to enable risk-management to function effectively. The designed purpose is to fund and sustain risk-management operations. Proper SERVES direction: servant (safety-investment) → master (risk-management).

Safety-observability is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: it provides the monitoring, data collection, and reporting that safety-management needs to make informed decisions and maintain oversight. The designed purpose is to feed safety-management with visibility. Proper SERVES direction: servant (safety-observability) → master (safety-management).

A clothing brand is a specific kind of trademark — a distinctive name, symbol, or design identifying clothing goods and their source. A competent speaker calls a clothing brand 'a trademark' (Law 9a). This avoids my past mistake of leaping to 'clothing' which is not its nearest kind.

Safety-exercise (drills, practices, and training routines) is maintained for the sake of safety-management: it provides the practical validation and skill-retention that safety-management relies on to verify plans work in reality. The designed purpose is to further safety-management's operation.

Emergency procedures (protocols for responding to safety incidents) are built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: they are the operational response component that safety-management designs and oversees. The designed purpose is to execute safety-management's crisis plans.

Hazard-reporting is maintained for the sake of hazard-assessment: it channels frontline hazard data into assessment processes where risks can be evaluated, prioritized, and acted upon. The reporting process serves the broader assessment function. Classic SERVES teleology — the servant (reporting) points at the master (assessment).

Exception-handling depends on baseline: to handle exceptions correctly, a system needs a known-good baseline state to restore to. Remove the baseline concept and exception-handling loses its recovery mechanism — it cannot restore system operation without a reference to the correct state.

Survivorship-bias is a specific kind of selection-bias: the bias that arises when only 'surviving' or observable cases are included in analysis, leading to systematic over-estimation of success. Test: survivorship-bias is a subset of selection-bias cases.

Safety-climate-survey serves safety-management: the survey is designed and maintained for the sake of safety-management. Its designed purpose is to produce data that safety-management uses to gauge organizational safety posture, identify trends, and make governance decisions. For-whose-sake test: survey→management (servant→master).

Safety-indicators are maintained for the sake of risk-management: they provide the quantitative data (leading, lagging, and critical metrics) that risk managers need to assess exposure, allocate resources, and make risk decisions.

Safety-signage (warning signs, hazard labels, directional markers) is designed specifically to help workers recognize hazards in their environment. Without signage, many hazards remain unnoticed until an incident occurs.

FMEA is a specific methodology for identifying potential failure modes and assessing their risks. It is a kind of risk-assessment — a competent speaker would call FMEA a form of risk assessment. Nearest kind check: risk-assessment is the proper parent category for FMEA.

Small multiples (Tufte's technique of displaying parallel small views of data) is designed for the sake of data visualization — it enables comparison across subsets of data, which is the core purpose of visualizing data. By design and sustained practice in statistics and information design.

Safety-indicators provide the quantitative metrics (leading, lagging, critical) that safety managers need to assess, monitor, and improve safety performance. Designed for the sake of safety-management, the SERVES direction is correct.

Safety-indicators provide data on leading and lagging safety metrics that feed directly into hazard identification and risk assessment. The indicators serve hazard-assessment by surfacing trends, near-misses, and conditions that signal emerging hazards.

Safety-indicators (training completion rates, safety meeting frequency, participation rates) measure the behavioral and attitudinal signals that constitute safety-climate. Indicators serve climate assessment by providing the data needed to gauge organizational safety attitudes.

Safety-reviews are conducted for the sake of safety-management: they provide findings and recommendations that managers use to improve the safety system. The designed purpose of a review is to serve the manager's oversight function.

A runbook is a specific kind of procedure — specifically, a documented step-by-step procedure for operational tasks. Any competent operator would describe a runbook as 'a procedure.' The nearest kind is procedure (not documentation, which is the format, or playbook, which is a different genre of procedure).

Safety audits are conducted for the sake of safety-management: they verify compliance, assess control effectiveness, and provide findings that managers use to improve safety performance. Designed purpose is clearly service to management oversight. SERVES direction: servant (safety-audit)→master (safety-management).

Safety reports are produced for the sake of safety-management: they document findings, track metrics, and provide data that managers need to assess and improve safety performance. Designed purpose is clearly service to oversight. SERVES direction: servant (safety-report)→master (safety-management).

A radial tree is a specific kind of diagram that displays hierarchical data in a circular, tree-like layout radiating from a central node. A competent speaker would call a radial tree 'a diagram.' The nearest kind is diagram (Law 9).

Safety training is conducted for the sake of safety management: it builds the competence and awareness that safety management frameworks require to operate. Per Law 8d, safety-training is the servant, safety-management is the master.

Safety observation is built for the sake of safety management — it provides the systematic data (observed behaviors, conditions, deviations) that safety management needs to operate. The servant (observation) points at the master (management).

Safety protection is built for the sake of safety management — it provides the engineered barriers and protective measures that safety management coordinates and deploys. The servant (protection) points at the master (management). Safety management needs protection mechanisms to operate; protection exists to serve management's safety goals.

Incident investigation is built for the sake of safety-management: its designed purpose is to feed root-cause findings and corrective actions back into the safety management system, closing the feedback loop that allows safety management to learn and adapt. The servant (investigation) points at the master (management).
Safety permits are designed for the sake of safety management — they are a control mechanism within the safety management system, ensuring hazardous work only proceeds after review.
Observation reports are designed for the sake of safety observation practice — they document findings so observations can be tracked and acted upon.
Safety competition is designed for the sake of safety management — competitive benchmarking drives improvement in safety performance, serving the broader safety management system.
Safety permits are designed for the sake of hazard assessment — a permit-to-work system ensures hazards are identified and assessed before hazardous work begins.

Clothing brands are built and maintained for the sake of commerce — they identify products, build recognition, and drive purchasing decisions. The designed purpose of a clothing brand is to serve commercial activity (Law 8d: for whose sake? clothing-brand → commerce).

Safety leadership is a specific kind of safety management practice — it is about inspiring, motivating, and guiding others toward safety excellence. The sense pinned: leadership as applied to the safety domain. 'X is a specific kind of Y' → INSTANCE_OF (Law 9). Safety leadership IS a kind of safety management.

Status quo is a specific kind of concept — the concept of the existing state of affairs. Pinned sense: status quo as a category of social/political/legal analysis referring to 'how things currently stand.' 'X is a specific kind of Y' → INSTANCE_OF (Law 9).

Safety audit is a specific kind of safety management — a systematic, independent examination of safety performance against criteria. A competent speaker calls a safety audit 'a kind of safety management activity.' Direction verified: specific (audit) → general (management). Safety-audit already SERVES safety-management; INSTANCE_OF pins its kind.

Safety training is a specific kind of safety management — structured educational activities designed to build safety knowledge and behavior. A competent speaker calls safety training 'a kind of safety management.' Direction verified: specific (training) → general (management). Safety-training already SERVES safety-management; INSTANCE_OF pins its kind.

Safety sampling is a specific kind of safety management — systematic collection and analysis of safety data (observations, measurements, audits) to inform management decisions. A competent speaker would call safety sampling 'a kind of safety management.' Direction verified: specific (sampling) → general (management).

The stakeholder concept in safety context depends on safety management — a stakeholder is defined by their interest in and relationship to the safety management system. Remove safety management and the stakeholder role in safety has no operational meaning.

Safety leadership is built and maintained for the sake of safety management — its designed purpose is to inspire, motivate, and guide others toward the safety excellence that safety management systems require. The servant (safety leadership) points at the master (safety management).

Safety sampling — systematic collection and analysis of safety data — is built for the sake of safety management. Its designed purpose is to inform management decisions about safety performance. The servant (safety sampling) points at the master (safety management).

Lessons learned — the practice of capturing insights from past incidents and projects — is built for the sake of safety management. Its designed purpose is to feed knowledge back into the safety management system so that lessons from failures and near-misses improve future safety performance.

Stakeholder-analysis serves safety-management by systematically identifying which individuals and groups are affected by safety decisions, enabling targeted safety interventions and communication. The designed purpose is to further safety management operation.

Exception-handling serves safety-management by providing a systematic approach to anticipating, responding to, and recovering from failures and deviations. Its designed purpose is to maintain operational safety when things go wrong.

Safety incentives are designed for the sake of safety management — they shape behavior to reduce incidents, which is a core safety management objective. Servant (safety-incentive) points at master (safety-management). By design and sustained organizational practice.

Safety metrics are collected and analyzed to inform safety management decisions, track progress, and drive improvements. The designed purpose of safety metric gathering is to support safety management's operation. Servant points at master.

Safety training equips workers with hazard identification skills, directly supporting hazard assessment operations. Hazard assessment depends on trained personnel to recognize and evaluate hazards — the designed purpose of this training component is to enable hazard assessment. Servant → master.

Stakeholder-analysis is a specific kind of analysis — a structured method for identifying and mapping affected parties. A competent speaker would call it 'an analysis.' Files against the nearest kind per Law 9 and Law 11e.

Stakeholder-analysis is built for the sake of decision-making — its designed purpose is to identify who is affected by a decision so that decisions can account for those stakeholders. Servant (analysis) points at master (decision-making) per Law 8d.

Failover is built and maintained for the sake of availability — its designed purpose is to keep a system running when a primary component fails. The servant (failover) points at the master (availability). Per Law 8d, this records the teleological relation: failover exists to further availability.

Failover is a specific kind of redundancy mechanism — a system design strategy where components are duplicated so that if one fails, another takes over. A competent speaker would call failover 'a form of redundancy.' Per Law 9, files against the nearest kind (redundancy).

Safety policies are drafted and maintained for the sake of safety governance — they operationalize governance objectives into enforceable rules. The designed purpose of safety policy is to further safety governance's operation. Servant (policy) points at master (governance), per Law 8d.

Stakeholders are identified and engaged for the sake of safety management — their interests and concerns must be accounted for in safety decisions and policies. Per Law 8d: the stakeholder concept serves safety management's operation by ensuring affected parties are mapped and considered.

Defensive depth (layered protection) is designed and maintained for the sake of safety management — its purpose is to provide multiple independent layers of defense so that safety management can ensure no single failure compromises the system.

Scenario planning is built and maintained for the sake of safety management — it prepares safety managers to anticipate and respond to plausible future safety events. Its designed purpose is to further safety management's operational readiness.

Traceability is designed and maintained for the sake of safety management — it enables tracking of causes, decisions, and corrective actions through the system lifecycle. Its designed purpose is to further safety management's ability to investigate and learn from events.

CI has no substance without version control: remove version control and CI stops operating entirely — there is nothing to merge, build, or test. Version control is the constitutive substrate that CI operates on.

Safety-management exists for the sake of protecting and serving stakeholders — its designed purpose is to identify, assess, and mitigate risks that affect those who have an interest in the organization's outcomes. Servant→master: safety-management points at stakeholder as its beneficiary.

Safety isolation is a safety practice designed for the sake of hazard mitigation — its purpose is to isolate people, equipment, or processes from identified hazards, thereby reducing harm risk. The removal test doesn't apply (SERVES not DEPENDS_ON); the 'for whose sake' test: safety isolation serves hazard mitigation, not the reverse.

Safety interlock is a device designed for the sake of hazard mitigation — it prevents equipment operation until safety conditions are satisfied, thereby preventing harm. The designed purpose (Law 8d) is to further hazard mitigation: servant (safety-interlock) points at master (hazard-mitigation).

Safety barrier is a physical or administrative control designed for the sake of hazard mitigation — it creates separation between hazards and people. Its designed purpose (Law 8d) is to further hazard mitigation: servant (safety-barrier) → master (hazard-mitigation).
A safety-committee is designed for the sake of ensuring safety-policy is implemented and maintained — its purpose is to oversee and promote compliance with organizational safety policies.

A safety-baseline-metric is designed for the sake of maintaining and verifying safety-baseline compliance. Its purpose is to measure whether the baseline's thresholds are met — the metric serves the baseline as its measurement instrument.

Safety incentives are designed for the sake of safety-baseline compliance: they motivate behaviors and decisions that keep organizational risk within acceptable thresholds. The incentive is the servant; the baseline is the master.

Safety incentives are designed for the sake of stakeholders: they motivate behaviors and decisions that keep organizational risk within acceptable thresholds, protecting and benefiting the people who have a stake in the organization's safety.

A safety-exit is a specific type of safety management mechanism: an engineered egress pathway built into facility design for evacuating occupants during emergencies. It is a concrete instance of safety management infrastructure.

Safety-sampling is designed for the sake of safety-baseline: sampling programs verify whether organizational practices maintain baseline compliance. The sampling mechanism serves the baseline by providing feedback on whether thresholds are met. Servant→master.

FMEA is a structured safety analysis methodology that was developed after and builds upon HAZOP. HAZOP (1963) predates FMEA's widespread industrial adoption. Both are systematic methods for identifying failure modes and hazards, with FMEA generalizing and formalizing the approach. Law 7: which existed first? HAZOP predates FMEA's industrial use and fed into it.
Safety incentive programs are designed and maintained to increase participation in safety education — the incentives exist for the sake of driving educational engagement and knowledge transfer.

Safety exits (emergency egress pathways built into facilities) are designed and maintained for the sake of safety-management: they provide the physical means of executing evacuation plans that are a core function of safety management systems.

FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) is a specific analytical method for identifying potential failure modes and their effects — it is a kind of risk assessment, specifically a structured, bottom-up technique.

Safety exits (emergency egress pathways) are built and maintained for the sake of emergency response: they provide the physical means of executing evacuation during emergencies. The designed purpose is to support emergency-response operations.

code-review is maintained for the sake of managing technical debt: its designed purpose is to catch defects, poor designs, and architectural drift before they enter the codebase, preventing them from accumulating as debt.

code-review is a specific kind of peer review: both involve a third party examining work before acceptance, but code-review specializes this to source code changes prior to merge. A competent speaker would call code-review a form of peer review.

code-review is maintained partly for the sake of knowledge management: it distributes domain knowledge across the team by exposing all members to code they might not otherwise read, building shared understanding as a designed purpose of the practice.

chart INSTANCE_OF diagram. A chart is a specific kind of diagram — a visual representation of data or information using graphical elements. A competent speaker would call a chart 'a diagram.' The diagram entry is the nearest kind; no intermediate rung exists between chart and diagram.
Emergency plan exists for the sake of risk management: its designed purpose is to prepare organized responses to crises, directly serving the operation of risk management.
refactoring is maintained for the sake of managing technical debt: its designed purpose is to improve internal code structure without changing external behavior, directly reducing accumulated debt.

Safety-learning is maintained for the sake of safety-management: its purpose is to feed lessons from incidents and audits back into organizational safety practice. Remove safety-learning and safety-management loses its feedback loop for continuous improvement. Direction: servant→master correct.

A radar chart is NOT a kind of pie chart — pie charts show parts of a whole as wedges of a circle. Radar charts display values on radial axes. This test checks whether the filing would be caught by the nearest-kind rule.

Safety-automation is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: automated controls, monitoring systems, and alarm mechanisms exist to extend safety-management's ability to maintain safety conditions without requiring continuous human oversight. Remove automation and safety-management still operates but at significantly reduced scope and speed. SERVES direction: servant (safety-automation) → master (safety-management).

Safety-data is maintained for the sake of safety-analysis: its entire purpose is to provide the raw material — incident records, audit results, sampling results, exposure measurements — that safety-analysis transforms into findings. Remove safety-data and safety-analysis has nothing to analyze. SERVES direction: servant (safety-data) → master (safety-analysis).

Safety-automation needs safety-data to operate right now: automated controls, sensors, and alarm systems require real-time data streams (measurements, incident alerts, thresholds) to function. Remove the data flow and the automation ceases to operate — this passes the Law 8 removal test.

A radial tree is a specific kind of graph: nodes are arranged in concentric circles radiating from a root, with edges drawn radially. It is a concrete instance of the general graph concept, where the radial layout is a structural convention, not a different ontological category.
